test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 12 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the difference between striated and smooth muscle cells?

options.text: All striated muscles work by reflex action as compared to smooth muscles.
Striated muscles lack nuclei while smooth muscles are binucleated
Smooth muscles are not connected to the nerves while striated muscles are connected.
Smooth muscles cannot contract at will, while voluntary muscles contract at will

solution:
The correct answer is __**Smooth muscles cannot contract at will, while voluntary muscles contract at will.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Striated muscles:**

__
 
• They are also known as skeletal muscles and are responsible for **voluntary movements.**
 
• The can **contract at will as they are voluntary **muscles.
 
• These are long-fiber muscles that, when examined under a microscope, are identified by oblique or transverse striations, or alternatively, arranged bands of light and dark.
 
• Each muscle cell has many sarcomeres, or arrays of overlapping thin and thick filaments, which give each muscle cell its unique look.

**Smooth muscles:**

 
• These non-striated muscles exhibit steady, rhythmic contractions that are **involuntary in nature**.
 
• They **cannot contract will as they are involuntary in nature.**
 
• They comprise spindle-shaped, narrow cells and a centrally located single nucleus.
 
• The lining of smooth muscles can be found in most internal organs and large sections of the digestive tract.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Cardiac Muscles:**

 
• **Cardiomyocytes **are specialized cells that comprise cardiac muscle.
 
• Muscle ventricles and atria are formed out of cardiomyocytes.
 
• They contract regularly to maintain the **heart's blood flow**.
 
• Cardiomyocytes depend on **actin and myosin **for contraction, which makes their structure crucial.
